newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Oct 18 (Reuter ) - Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Friday.

"The interbank rate continued to rise today but there was minimal impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.55/2.50 compared with Thursday's yield of 2.40/2.35 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.10/2.05 percent against 1.94/1.89 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$97.88/97.93 from Thursday's close of S$98.17/98.22, September 2001 at S$97.72/97.77 versus S$98.35/98.40 and June 2003 at S$96.70/96.75 against S$97.37/97.42.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-11/16 3-9/16 percent from Thursday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
